title: Wrong Turn
full_review:
A group of oversexed twentysomething slackers find themselves on the road trip from hell, as they flee a trio of flesh.hungry, homicidal hillbillies in the schlocky gorefest "Wrong Turn" (Fox).

Buckets of blood flow in this formulaic clunker directed by Rob Schmidt, who succeeds in killing off viewers' interest as readily as he kills off his cardboard cast. In truth, it is Schmidt, not the axe.wielding berserkers, who is guilty of the real hack job here.

The plot -- if that is not too dignified a term .. is pure slasher 101. First you need a chiseled lead like Chris Flynn (Desmond Harrington), a young medical student on his way to an important interview in Raleigh. Then an obstacle, a jackknifed truck jamming traffic on the highway fits the bill nicely. This initiates a bad decision: leaving the safety of the highway to take a back.road detour cutting through a stretch of remote West Virginia wilderness. Flynn is soon lost and stops to ask for directions at a gas station where the toothless proprietor offers him the compulsory y'all-be-careful-now warning.

Next the recipe calls for victims since every slasherphile knows it is only etiquette that the star stays alive to see the end credits. This proves easy enough, since Flynn's car coincidentally crashes into a van full of marooned campers .. young, attractive campers at that .. whose tires were blown by barbed.wire snare strung like a trip.cord across the dirt road. They instantly bond and agree to split into the two requisite slasher groups. The first, also known as the "leads," go to fetch help, leaving behind the second less fortunate group, recognized as the "expendables." Meanwhile the cinematic sacrificial lambs do what expendables are paid to do, namely, die horrible deaths at the hands of the film's redneck cretins.

Meanwhile, Flynn and his new best friends, who include Clay (Jeremy Sisto), his fiancee, Carly (Emmanuelle Chriqui), and her conveniently unattached friend, Jesse (Eliza Dushku), stumble across a ramshackle cabin and decide to investigate; all professional slasher thespians seem prone to inexplicably poor judgment. Undeterred by the neo.Hannibal Lecter decor, replete with a refrigerator full of human body parts, they linger long enough for the maniac moonshiners to return home with the grizzly remains of their friends in tow. Through an opening.credit montage of news clippings viewers learn that the psychos du jour are a brood of cannibalistic backwater goobers, grotesquely disfigured by inbreeding.

The remainder of the film is a tedious cat.and.mouse game between the hunters and the hunted, made laughable by tired references to "Deliverance." It is never a question of whether someone will get killed, but only who will get done in first and by what ghoulish means: arrow through the eye, garroted by barbed wire, or the always popular axe to the head?

The film quickly plummets from the repulsive to the utterly ridiculous, setting up a predictable can't.keep.a.good.inbred.maniac.down finale, with several false endings sure to send popcorn flying. The whole messy affair is punctuated by a big boom and an obligatory end.credit capper which leaves the door open for an even bloodier sequel.

True to the genre's two.note repertoire of shock and disgust, the filmmaker seems gleefully content with assaulting audiences with a sickening barrage of gross images and gratuitously graphic violence. To its credit, except for some lewd humor and an implied, sexual encounter, the film is not as sexually exploitive as other past slasher flicks. In fact, the only thing bare is the film's script, as in threadbare.

A warning for parents or any viewer actually considering plunking down cash for this mindless dreck: The only wrong turn you can make is into the theater.

Due to excessive graphic violence, recurring rough language, an implied sexual encounter, lewd humor and drug abuse, the USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is O .. morally offensive. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R .. restricted.
